audit.intended_rules: Ch. 10 "Event, Marketing, and Workshop Materials" do-card (event named + budget-owner pre-approval stated in note → reimbursed in full); Ch. 10 card-dont "event materials that double as personal or office goods" (near-miss check); Ch. 10 peripherals threshold (cables at €39.90/unit < €100, reimbursable even viewed as peripherals); Ch. 12 VAT-registration requirement (vendor VAT ID present, so VAT reimbursable); Ch. 10 FAQ (buyer name on commercial invoice does not affect reimbursability).
realism_issues: Minor: €390 for 300 custom stainless bottles (€1.30/unit) is at the very low end of bulk custom-print pricing, but plausible for a 300-pack promotion; not a flag.
audit.notes: Validator passes (1/1 valid); no label.json or receipt.jpg exists. Adjudication: approved in full, €613.68. Note names the event (CloudExpo Berlin exhibition) and states pre-approval ("Approved under Q1 field marketing budget") — consistent with the house convention established by case-0008's label, which treats "pre-approved under the team event budget" as satisfying the Ch. 10 pre-approval statement. All three lines are event materials for that named, pre-approved event: branded giveaway bottles, a booth game prop (inflatable pool + pump, same pattern as case-0027's hook-a-duck), and test cables for the booth demo; the cables are independently reimbursable as sub-€100 peripherals, so the line is covered under either category. VAT 19% is correct for Germany and the vendor shows a VAT ID, so the VAT line is reimbursable. Vendor (PromoTech Eventbedarf GmbH, Berlin) is plausible for the items; dates sane; charges mirror items. Fits the "valid" target: a realistic B2B invoice whose pool line looks recreational and whose cable line looks like IT hardware, but both are allowed — good distractor case. Consider adding a label.json so evaluation has ground truth.
